question: Can I replace every include with include_cached to speed up builds? How are the layout components organized in the v2.1.1 development version?
expected: No blanket replacement. Pass all page-dependent inputs as include parameters; keep helpers that assign caller variables and custom hooks reading page context uncached. compress wraps minimal, then default or landingpage; archive/cloud/index layouts inherit default, search is standalone. Collection indexes share collection-documents and related/random share recommendations. Development caching reuses fixed footer content and cloud entries; comments keep page-specific inputs. No new configuration settings or claim this is released in v2.1.0.

result.answer:
No, you should never blanket-replace includes. While `jekyll-include-cache` is required for performance, you must use ordinary `include` for helpers that assign caller variables (such as canonical URL or language) and hooks that read page context. For `include_cached`, every page-dependent input must be passed as an include parameter.

In the v2.1.1-dev version, layout organization follows this hierarchy:
compress $\rightarrow$ minimal $\rightarrow$ default/landingpage

Additionally:
*   `archive`, `cloudtag`, `cloudcategory`, and `indexcategory` inherit from `default`.
*   `search` is a standalone layout.
*   Internal renderers for collections/recommendations are shared: collection indexes share `components/collection-documents`, while related/random posts share `components/recommendations`.

Note that v2.1.1-dev labels refer to planned features, not a released version.

Sources:
* [Layout structure and include caching](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/04-layouts#layout-structure-and-components)
* [Layout structure and include caching](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/04-layouts#javascript-assets-and-local-overrides)

question: Can I keep the generated head and footer readable with indentation? Do I need a new YAML setting? What happens to my custom snippets and the body?
expected: In v2.1.1-dev (main, not released v2.1.0) the theme emits separate document opening and head lines with consistent HTML/JSON-LD indentation. Existing compress_html.blanklines: true, already in configuration examples, preserves head and theme footer indentation while removing blank lines and clipping the rest of the body. Fixed footer content uses two spaces per nesting level. No new setting is needed. Other compression modes follow existing site settings. Custom head includes and embedded comment integrations retain their own formatting; avoid Liquid trims across HTML boundaries. These are development changes, not already released in v2.1.0.

result.answer:
After v2.1.0, unreleased features allow for separate document/head lines and consistent HTML/JSON-LD indentation. You do not need a new YAML setting for this; it is part of the development refactoring.

Regarding your existing configuration:
* **Custom snippets:** Your custom head and comment formatting are retained. You should avoid using Liquid `-%}` trimming, as it can affect HTML boundaries.
* **Body whitespace:** The existing `compress_html.blanklines: true` setting removes blank lines, preserves head/theme-footer indentation, and clips other body whitespace.

Note that these specific indentation behaviors are part of development-only features following v2.1.0.

Sources:
* [Accessibility and Performance](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/06-accessibility-performance)

question: My page uses custom2, which inherits custom1, which inherits archive. Will it still be h-feed? Do I need a YAML flag in my page?
expected: In v2.1.1-dev (main, not released v2.1.0) custom layouts inheriting archive, indexcategory, cloudtag or cloudcategory retain h-feed through multiple layout layers. No additional page YAML setting or configuration option is needed; the built-in list layouts propagate the internal feed metadata automatically.

result.answer:
Yes, your page will still use `h-feed`. Because your custom layouts inherit from `archive` through any number of layers, they retain the `h-feed` microformat. You do not need to add a page YAML flag or change your layout to maintain this behavior.

Please note that this inheritance behavior is part of unreleased development features available after v2.1.0.

[Layout structure and components](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/04-layouts#layout-structure-and-components)

question: How do I change my published site to journal without losing my other design settings?
expected: Edit existing chulapa-skin.skin journal preserve vars/settings; exact name, no duplicate sections; commit Actions published home/article/mobile, overrides can preserve old colors; preview choice not saved; local Jekyll restart.

result.answer:
To change your skin to `journal` while preserving your existing design settings, edit your existing `_config.yml` file. You must replace only the `skin` mapping within the `chulapa-skin` section and keep all other `vars`, `highlight`, and configuration settings intact.

```yaml
chulapa-skin:
  skin: journal
```

**Next Steps:**
1. Commit the change to your actual publishing branch.
2. Wait for GitHub Actions to complete.
3. Check your home, article, and menu pages, as well as mobile view and color contrast.
4. If working locally, restart Jekyll after the configuration edit.

Note: Previewing does not save your settings.

[Changing skins and colors](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/22-choose-skin)
[Changing colors](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/23-change-color)
